package.title: Frontier Models — 7月の世代交代
package.editorial_angle: GPT-5.6、Claude Opus 5、Gemini 3.6 Flash、DeepSeek V4-Flash、Kimi K3を単純ランキングせず、公開形態・価格・API・open-weight性・agent/coding接続という異なる競争軸で比較する。
boundaries: Benchmark, efficiency, and estimated-cost comparisons are largely vendor-reported and depend on effort levels, harnesses, token usage, and pricing assumptions; they should not be flattened into a universal ranking.

Architecture scale, capability comparisons, and benchmark positioning are vendor claims from the Kimi documentation; open-source status should be interpreted using the actual published license/weights when drafting.

claims.text: OpenAI launched the GPT-5.6 family for general availability on July 9, 2026 with Sol, Terra, and Luna tiers across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API.
The release introduced Programmatic Tool Calling in the Responses API and a multi-agent beta; OpenAI's `ultra` setting coordinates parallel agents for demanding tasks.
OpenAI later reduced GPT-5.6 Luna pricing by 80% and Terra pricing by 20% on July 30.
Performance-per-dollar and benchmark superiority claims in the launch and follow-up articles are OpenAI/vendor claims even when they reference third-party benchmarks.

limitations.text: Benchmark, efficiency, and estimated-cost comparisons are largely vendor-reported and depend on effort levels, harnesses, token usage, and pricing assumptions; they should not be flattened into a universal ranking.

claims.text: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026 and made it available across its platforms and API that day.
Anthropic priced Opus 5 at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens and positioned it as the new default on Claude Max and the strongest model on Claude Pro.
Anthropic reports Opus 5 as close to Fable 5 frontier capability at lower cost and presents broad coding, knowledge-work, science, and safety evaluation gains.

limitations.text: Benchmark and alignment comparisons are primarily Anthropic-reported; individual evaluation harnesses and partner testimonials are not equivalent to independent replication.

claims.text: DeepSeek's changelog records the DeepSeek-V4-Flash API as entering public beta on July 31, 2026 under the model name `deepseek-v4-flash`.
DeepSeek states that the July 31 build keeps the architecture and size of V4-Flash-Preview and changes post-training only.
An April 24 migration notice scheduled the legacy `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` names for discontinuation on July 24, 2026.

limitations.text: DeepSeek's benchmark scores for V4-Flash are vendor-reported and include a specified DeepSeek Harness configuration; this card treats the July lifecycle and API change as the primary fact.

claims.text: Google made Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite generally available on July 21, 2026.
On July 30 Google added Gemini Robotics ER 2 and a streaming variant in public preview, with multimodal inputs and function calling for robotics workflows.
Google describes Gemini 3.6 Flash as improving token efficiency and code/agentic planning while lowering price relative to 3.5 Flash.

limitations.text: Capability/efficiency positioning is Google-reported; the July release-notes page establishes model lifecycle and availability rather than independent benchmark superiority.

claims.text: Kimi Code's official changelog records Kimi K3 as released and open-sourced on July 16, 2026 and available in Kimi Code.
Moonshot describes Kimi K3 as a 2.8-trillion-parameter model using KDA hybrid linear attention and Attention Residuals, with native visual understanding and up to a 1M-token context window.
The same July 16 Kimi Code release aligned the coder sub-agent with background tasks, plan mode, skills, and nested-agent capabilities.

limitations.text: Architecture scale, capability comparisons, and benchmark positioning are vendor claims from the Kimi documentation; open-source status should be interpreted using the actual published license/weights when drafting.
